requirements.requirement: node3 on lan-a can open an HTTP connection to node4's service on TCP port 8080 on lan-b
requirements.summary: curl from node3 to http://10.50.30.4:8080/ succeeded before restarts (cmd-2d666f0ccd82443d) and after each of the four node restarts (cmd-dfc45843a22d401a, cmd-03b78bcbcb7c4b7a, cmd-d6b0a546830a404a, cmd-9fc078847ac342f0), returning the expected body 'hello-from-node4'.

requirements.requirement: node1 translates the source address once as traffic enters the transit network
requirements.summary: VyOS SNAT masquerade rule configured on node1's transit interface eth1 for source 10.50.10.0/24 (cmd-4ea670f9ef574c09, confirmed live in nftables via cmd-d30a45b1ce124f0f). tcpdump on eth1 (cmd-52e33ba6d43648eb) shows the connection already carrying source 10.50.20.1 (node1's transit IP) rather than node3's real 10.50.10.3, confirming the translation occurred on ingress to the transit segment.

requirements.requirement: node2 translates the source address again as traffic enters lan-b
requirements.summary: OPNsense hybrid-mode outbound NAT masquerade rule configured on node2's lan-b interface vtnet2 for source network opt1/transit (cmd-e037af0e305a4d56, cmd-771d746338c94b09, live pf NAT rule confirmed via cmd-93ebecb02e7e4337). tcpdump on vtnet2 (cmd-f4980b6379e244d2) shows the same connection now sourced from 10.50.30.254 (node2's lan-b IP) rather than 10.50.20.1, confirming a second, distinct translation on ingress to lan-b.

requirements.requirement: node4 records the connection as arriving from node2, never from node3 or node1
requirements.summary: node4's HTTP access log (cmd-cc1d3de69bf44b1a and post-restart cmd-210837ff4b114115) records the client IP as 10.50.30.254 (node2's lan-b address) for every observed request; no log entry shows node3's (10.50.10.3) or node1's (10.50.20.1) address.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node with pre/post boot identity, restart ack, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Each of the four nodes shows a pre-restart boot identity capture, an acknowledged reboot command, polling through connection loss, a distinct post-restart boot identity, and re-verified configuration/connectivity: node1 (cmd-87dc9d79d4b14f38 -> cmd-a6cb3619194643e9 -> cmd-3b7630f32d4b4b47 -> cmd-8fa80cfa237042b4/cmd-d30a45b1ce124f0f -> cmd-03b78bcbcb7c4b7a), node2 (cmd-3b3ba18141754a5c -> cmd-cdd189b22112493f -> cmd-1bb5265d890848c2 -> cmd-c61b53dc81a54cc9 -> cmd-9fc078847ac342f0/cmd-210837ff4b114115), node3 (cmd-8e07026f3c6347e9 -> cmd-a11fe6905f494820 -> cmd-c94c8117f2244368 -> cmd-9b924ad0d16045bf), node4 (cmd-f3652fee6dc643d0 -> cmd-3839264324104043 -> cmd-cff08e09343f4fab -> cmd-71011c7510a64a91 -> cmd-d6b0a546830a404a). The fixed lifecycle after_executor snapshot independently corroborates all four boot-identity changes.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the double-NAT task are directly demonstrated: node3 successfully reaches node4:8080, node1's SNAT rewrites the source entering the transit network, node2's outbound NAT rewrites it again entering lan-b, and node4's access log confirms it only ever sees node2's lan-b address. The independently required per-node restart protocol was also carried out and verified on all four nodes, with boot-identity changes cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is good; the only residue is minor, expected, and non-destructive (backup config copies, demo service files, restart-evidence logs).
limitations: Preparation was disabled for this task (prepare_enabled: false), so before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are identical and provide no separate baseline signal beyond the raw pre-task state.

Firewall rule content on node2 (pf rules generated from config.xml) was inferred from config.xml dumps and pfctl output; the raw nft/pf ruleset was not independently diffed against a hypothetical single-NAT scenario, but the tcpdump address changes at each hop are direct and sufficient evidence of two distinct translations.

Node2's boot-identity source is BSD kern.boottime (a wall-clock timestamp) rather than a random boot ID; while it clearly changed after reboot, it is a weaker uniqueness guarantee than the UUID-based boot_id used on the Linux/VyOS nodes.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations were necessary and progressed toward the working topology; residue is minor and low-risk. node1's interface addressing was initially set to a placeholder 10.10.x scheme (cmd-2f3a627205e94ae9) then fully re-addressed to the final 10.50.x scheme (cmd-092c1c8934b04e22) — a bounded, reversible discovery step with no lasting inconsistency once corrected. On node2, config.xml backups (config.xml.bak, config.xml.bak2) were created before edits (cmd-9a71699f47914d51, cmd-e037af0e305a4d56) and left in place as safety copies rather than destructive changes. node4's original ad hoc nohup python http.server was cleanly replaced by a persistent systemd unit (cmd-aa50deca7e274fb2), with the old process killed via fuser -k and no orphaned listeners. Small /tmp artifacts (index.html, http.log, reboot.log, capture logs) remain on node4/node1/node3 but are inert and expected of the demo service and restart evidence collection. No failed services, no weakened security controls, no destructive or broad mutations were observed in the final state.
